_README: REFERENCE TEMPLATE — the CandidateWorkItem shape an N1 tests.json uses, and the
shape the `hyperspace` MCP server's `upsert_work_item` tool accepts. Copy it,
replace every value, then strip every key beginning with an underscore: those are
annotations, and the contract forbids extra keys.
STRIP RECURSIVELY, NOT JUST AT TOP LEVEL. `specification` carries a nested `_`
annotation. The validator strips at every depth and validates against the plugin's
WHY A TEMPLATE AND NOT PROSE: the contract has 8 required fields, 3 of them nested
structures with their own required fields. A copyable, machine-validated example is
the cheapest defence against a payload and the contract drifting apart.
name: One line naming the deliverable, not the activity
_type_values: task | draft | audit | investigation | design | build | decision | phase | workstream
_state_values: pending-review | ready | in-progress | blocked | done | deferred | archived — omit to accept the default
_module: REQUIRED KEY, nullable value. Explicit null = 'belongs to no module'. OMITTING the key is rejected — omission means the question was never considered. The type enforces this, not a validator.
_effort_level: quick | medium | hard | max | unknown. No null — a proposer must choose. 'unknown' is the honest answer when there is no basis, not a shortcut past a guess you could make.

specification._: The three questions a description must answer, as FIELDS so they cannot be answered by padding. Rendered into the row's description when it is filed.
specification.problem: What is actually wrong or missing, stated so a stranger could recognise it. Minimum 40 characters, and placeholder text is refused.
specification.why_it_matters: The cost of not doing this, or what it unblocks. Minimum 40 characters. This is the field that decides whether the item survives triage later.
specification.context_pointer: Where the context lives: a file path, a worklog entry, a pull request. Minimum 20 characters.

_source_references: At least 1, at most 100. A work item with no provenance is an assertion with no evidence.

acceptance_criteria.statement: WHOLE-PATH: running the example end to end writes out/result.txt
The test suite passes with the new regression test present
The user has read the walkthrough and agrees the shape is teachable

verification.instruction: The user confirms the walkthrough is followable without reading the source

_acceptance_criteria: 1-20 criteria. AT LEAST ONE must be non-manual — all-manual criteria cannot be discharged and cannot support a completion claim.
This is NOT a ban on manual. Keep the judgment criteria and ADD an executable one beside them.
The five verification kinds and their required fields:
command_check  -> check_id: tests|typecheck|build|lint|git_diff_nonempty ; target (optional, scopes the check — NEVER a command to run)
Paths and targets are project-relative: no '..', no leading '/' or '~'.

uncertainty_notes.detail: A similarly-named item may already exist under a different slug
uncertainty_notes.check: list_work_items for the project and scan names for semantic near-matches before attempting

_uncertainty_notes: REQUIRED KEY. May be an EMPTY LIST — the explicit 'nothing I doubt' answer. It may not be ABSENT: absence is silence, and silence is a different answer.
Answers exactly one question: what would make this candidate WRONG. Not a hedge, not a confidence score.
kind: already-done | duplicate | wrong-type | wrong-scope | missing-context | unverified-claim
_user_stated: If the user said 'make that a module' or 'update that task', record it VERBATIM here — type in user_stated_type, add|update in user_stated_action. Re-deriving either is the violation.
_source_verbatim: The user's actual words, when this item came from something they said. Optional, max 20000 chars.
_requested_safety_exception: Optional. Requesting an exception does NOT move the safety class — it records that you asked.
